newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday on talk the market would be merged into a unified national state debt trading market based in Beijing, traders said.
The most active three-day contract fell to 6.72 percent from 7.01 percent on Wednesday. Combined volume of the six-contract market rose to 5.39 million lots from 2.57 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said market talk was that China would open a unified state debt market in the second half of 1997 and the Shanghai state debt market would merge with other similar markets China.

"Big institutions used the rumours as an excuse to sell on the markets today," said one trader. "This depressed market sentiment, and that depressed the repo rates despite two new listings on the (domestic) A share markets."
Traders said if the rumours were not officially denied, they would continue to circulate on the market, dampening sentiment and further depressing the repo rates.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday on strong sentiment, traders said.
